column2: The Call of the Dark Gods

The skalds sing of Kjörn and Loesh, of Nierg and Tchar, and of the Snow King and the Great Bear beside them, as if all of them were the same. They are not. The old gods of the north grow fat on our gifts and give nothing back. The Dark Gods give. They give strength to the strong, wisdom to the cunning and long life to those who do not flinch from rot.\n\nI have heard their call long enough. Tonight I burn the old totems and give myself to the true powers of the world. To which of them shall I swear?

The herd has bellowed to all the Dark Gods alike, and the Dark Gods have answered all of us alike. That is no longer enough for me. One of them has whispered to me alone, and the warband that serves that god has marked me as its own. It is time to give my whole soul to one master.
Blood for the Blood God! Skulls for the Skull Throne!
Slaanesh will grant me every desire.
This world reeks of death. Grandfather Nurgle will keep me.
Everyone plots against me. The Changer of Ways shows me their plots.
All of them! For the Dark Gods, for Chaos Undivided!
Not tonight.

At the runestone above the fjord the godi has laid out the totems of the north: the bull of Kjörn, the serpent of Loesh, the toad of Nierg, the raven of Tchar, the wolf of Olric and the bear of Órsen. A chieftain gives gifts to all the gods, but the greatest chieftains raise one god above the rest, and that god walks beside them in battle.\n\nThe law of my realm lets me raise only some of them. Whose totem shall I take up?
The bull. Kjörn, Lord of Battle, give me blood and skulls.
The serpent. Loesh will give me everything I crave.
The toad. Nierg, Father of Plagues, make me endure.
The raven. Tchar sees every secret and every road.
The wolf. Olric, Snow King, High King of the gods.
The bear. Órsen, Father of Bears, give me courage.
Not yet. All the gods shall have their gifts a while longer.

Early in the morning, you and a band of your closest warriors are hunting a stag, along the way you stumble upon an idol to Tchar. Your companions are scouting ahead of you when the idol begins speaking to you, promising absolute power and dominion over all others, if you only worship him...

Lately, you've noticed yourself becoming more and more aggressive, and constantly craving for battle and glory. Your slumber is disturbed when Kharneth, the Blood God, demands that you join his ranks, and forever live in glory.

You are walking through your hall during a slow day. After participating in a great feast and round of drinking that would make a legendary tale in itself, you still feel empty inside, like something is missing. Soon, you begin hearing voices, beautiful ones, calling to you, asking you to give yourself to Shornaal so that you may be satisfied...

In your dreams Nurgleth, Lord of Death and Decay calls to you... 'The world is falling, it is corrupt, dying... embrace it, my child... embrace your destiny...' you hear a voice calling, and maggots crawl up from the ground, greeting you...

In your dreams, spirits of all shapes and forms come to you... You recognise many of them, and they press on you, whispering forbidden secrets and promises of power. They demand that you cast off the deities and guardians that have guided you your whole life and devote yourself entirely to the real gods of this world, the Dark Gods of Chaos Undivided: Khorne, Nurgle, Tzeentch & Slaanesh.

Unlike the southerners, northern realms barely recognize the hereditary customs of the south. Being a follower of Khorne, you must be strong and blood-thirsty in order to gain the respect of the clans, something you are not.

Unlike the southerners, northern realms barely recognize the hereditary customs of the south, where only the strong may lead. You have been deemed a weak individual by the clans, and thus they refuse to recognise your authority.

Unlike the southerners, northern realms barely recognize the hereditary customs of the south. Being a follower of Slaanesh, you must woo and impress your clansmen to gain their respect, something you are incapable of doing.

Unlike the southerners, northern realms barely recognize the hereditary customs of the south. Being a follower of Tzeentch, you must be intelligent, skilled in statecraft, or have some skill in magic, but you have none of these.

Unlike the southerners, northern realms barely recognize the hereditary customs of the south. Being a follower of Nurgle, you must be kind and charitable, spreading Nurgle's love to all, but you are greedy, and keep Nurgle's joys to yourself.

Unlike the southerners, northern realms barely recognize the hereditary customs of the south, and as such, unless the heir is clearly favored by their gods, the realm will dissolve on the leaders death. Your heir currently does not show any favor at all, and unless they were to improve, your realm will dissolve upon your death.

Tchar is known to be a trickster...
Glory in battle is a fine thing, but I shall earn it myself.
And end up a decadent sluggard? I think not!
Wreck and ruin to Nurgleth, I shall make my own way!
My oaths to my kin and my gods are too important to betray!
Alas, it is as the gods demand it.
I must shape them up before I die...
I shall be a willing servant to Tchar, Changer of Ways!
Yes... Yes! Blood for the Blood God!
More... More of everything!
May the corpse trail grow long!
For the Ruinous Powers!
I am aware of my culture's traditions, bother me no more of this!

Your heir must be an adult, and the clans follow the heir's own god:
-Khorne: 888 prestige, 15 martial, strength, a gift of Khorne or a great general, and never soft, weak, frail or kind
-Slaanesh: 666 prestige or piety, 15 diplomacy or intrigue, beauty or a taste for pleasure, and never ugly, fat or disfigured
-Nurgle: 777 piety, 15 stewardship, kindness, charity or an ugly face, and never greedy or cruel
-Tzeentch: 999 prestige, 15 learning or intrigue, a quick mind, magic or a mutation, and never dull, wroth or honest
-The old gods, Undivided, Olric and Orsen: 555 piety or prestige, 15 martial or diplomacy, strength, wisdom or a gift of Chaos, and never soft, weak or frail
Otherwise the great vassals break away when you die.
